frozen_inputs.separator: fit_gold_indicators.separation — mean(z | trough windows) - mean(z | peak windows). The separator itself never applies abs(); abs() is applied by the capture rule, which fits direction per indicator and records it as +1 (trough-high/peak-low) or -1 (inverted)
frozen_inputs.grids: fit_gold_indicators.indicator_grid — the Plan-19 frozen grids, imported not restated; no grid changed after seeing output. Every grid row is handed to the module, which selects the row maximising |separation| (the harness's best_overall keys on the signed value)
frozen_inputs.anchor: valuation = shipped rolling_z rails, rolling 90d / z 1.0, scored as one more row

windows_label: detector turns -> +/-45d cycle windows (turns_to_cycle_windows). A SCORING TARGET only: no exposure floor, no execution period, no perfect-strategy oracle.
in_sample_label: IN-SAMPLE: every separation is fit against the same detected turns it is measured on, at every bar with a valid z. This calibrates indicator windows to detected history; it is NOT out-of-sample predictive skill and the holdout stays spent and untouched.

provisional.note: bar applied, direction-stability veto NOT applied — a per-row/level view, not the settled count the choice was ranked by

choice.capture_rule: An indicator's row is the grid row maximising |separation|. It CAPTURES a level iff |separation| >= 0.5 z-units AND is not degenerate (neither window side's mean inside +/-0.06). abs() IS applied to the bar — this REVERSES the earlier 'abs() is forbidden' rule, because direction is now FITTED per indicator and recorded as +1 (trough-high / peak-low) or -1 (inverted) rather than imposed. DIRECTION STABILITY: an indicator capturing at more than one level must carry the SAME fitted direction at every level where it captures; a flip is flagged direction_unstable, captures nowhere, and the flip is recorded. An unscoreable leg never captures.
choice.choice_rule: Sensitivity crank: a lower min_move_pct yields MORE turns, so a smaller min_move_pct is the MORE SENSITIVE (finer) calibration. A level QUALIFIES iff its capture count is at least as large as at every COARSER level (it loses no indicator relative to the coarser calibrations); the coarsest level therefore always qualifies. Among qualifiers take the one with the LARGEST capture_depth — the SUM of the capturing indicators' |separation| at that level. The ranking key is DEPTH, NOT HEADCOUNT: a knife-edge indicator that clears the bar by 0.0042 must not be able to hand the decision to a different granularity, and under headcount it counts as one vote exactly like a deeply-separating leg. Capture count is still reported, it just does not rank. Where two qualifiers reach the SAME capture_depth prefer the COARSER one (fewer turns, more robust).
choice.rationale: the most sensitive granularity the indicators can still capture: finer pin sets are harder scoring targets, so sensitivity is taken as far as the indicator evidence carries it and no further. Among the levels the indicators do carry, the one they carry DEEPLY wins, because headcount cannot tell a vote held from conviction from one held by 0.0042
